Bhante, in 'web books meditations13 section0008 html 5c8533' (web books meditations13 section0008 html 5c8533), what is the core doctrinal teaching regarding '[Section: Strong Through Mindfulness] Most of'?

In this section from *web books meditations13 section0008 html 5c8533*, the master explains: *"[Section: Strong Through Mindfulness] Most of us learn about mindfulness starting with mindfulness meditation, mindfulness of breathing, the four foundations or establishings of mindfulness."*. From the perspective of the Four Noble Truths, suffering arises whenever the mind grasps at impermanent phenomena (*anicca*) as a reliable self (*atta*). By establishing clear comprehension (*sampajañña*) and seeing conditioned events as empty of inherent ownership, craving (*taṇhā*) is unhooked. It is like grasping a poisonous cobra by the tail: tempting and sleek from afar, but deadly the moment you grasp it. Release the tail and live in safety. Anchor your understanding in direct seeing rather than speculative theory.

Rest the mind gently in the rhythm of each natural in-and-out breath.
